sample_unit: surgical cases (evaluation set; plus 500 external validation cases)

links.outcome: LLM case length prediction error and accuracy versus current OR scheduling estimates on the same cases
links.effect: Fine-tuned GPT-4 MAE 47.64 min vs current scheduling 49.34 min (P = .10, matching); accuracy within 20% was 46.12% vs 40.92% (P < .001).
links.quote: Both GPT-4 fine-tuned and GPT-3.5 fine-tuned significantly outperformed current scheduling methods in accuracy (46.12% and 46.08% vs 40.92%, respectively; P < .001).

links.outcome: Prediction error of fine-tuned versus non-fine-tuned LLMs using institutional case data
links.effect: Fine-tuned GPT-4 MAE 47.64 min vs best base model (GPT-4) MAE 59.20 min; fine-tuned GPT-4 also performed best in external validation (MAE 48.66 min).
links.quote: Base models demonstrated variable performance, with GPT-4 showing the highest performance among non-fine-tuned models (MAE, 59.20 minutes; 95% CI, 56.88 - 61.52).

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation and external validation of multiple LLMs to predict surgical case length from clinical text, comparing against current scheduling estimates.
